delegates.ConstantFoldBinaryOpOperands: foldOrCommuteConstant with both operands constant, IS.foldOrCommuteConstant.L582: the constant folder, not modelled
delegates.simplifyAndOrOfCmps: and/or of two icmps, looking through casts of one opcode from one type: another family's fold (simplifyAndOfICmps, simplifyOrOfICmps), not modelled here; the model hands over only where both operands are icmps after the look-through
delegates.simplifyAssociativeBinOp: recursive calls to simplifyBinOp with MaxRecurse - 1, not modelled; the model hands over where MaxRecurse isn't 0 and the first simplifyBinOp of one of its transforms may answer, which Logic.Ext.simplifies says. Logic.Ext.ofTerms, as onInst has it, says each may, so it hands over wherever an operand has the opcode
delegates.expandCommutativeBinOp: recursive calls to simplifyBinOp with MaxRecurse - 1, not modelled; the model hands over where MaxRecurse isn't 0 and expandBinOp's first simplifyBinOp may answer, which Logic.Ext.simplifies says. Logic.Ext.ofTerms says each may, so it hands over wherever an operand has the opcode it distributes over
delegates.threadBinOpOverSelect: recursive calls to simplifyBinOp with MaxRecurse - 1, not modelled; the model hands over where MaxRecurse isn't 0, an operand is a select, and the operation on one of its values may simplify, which Logic.Ext.simplifies says. Logic.Ext.ofTerms says it may
delegates.threadBinOpOverPHI: recursive calls to simplifyBinOp with MaxRecurse - 1 over a phi's incoming values, not modelled; a phi is an opaque Term (Term.var), so with no Logic.Ext the model hands over where MaxRecurse isn't 0 and an operand is opaque, and with one, where Logic.Ext.isPhi says it's a phi. Logic.Ext.ofTerms says no opaque operand is, as in the functions compare builds, whose opaque operands are arguments
delegates.simplifyByDomEq: shared with sub, udiv, sdiv, urem and srem, and its sites (IS.simplifyByDomEq.L727, L736) aren't this family's; it answers only at MaxRecurse == RecursionLimit, and only where isImpliedByDomCondition says Op0 == Op1, which Logic.Ext.domEq answers. With no Ext the model hands over at the top level; Logic.Ext.ofTerms says no condition dominates, as in the functions compare builds
delegates.isCheckForZeroAndMulWithOverflow: the overflow bit isn't a Term (see unproved); with no Logic.Ext the model hands over where an operand is opaque and the other an icmp of the right predicate against 0, and with one, where Logic.Ext.isMulOverflowBit says the opaque operand is the bit. Logic.Ext.ofTerms says it isn't
delegates.simplifyWithOpReplaced: with no Logic.Ext, the model hands over where Op0 is an equality icmp or trunc nuw to i1; with one, its answer is a parameter, see rests_on. Logic.Ext.ofTerms, as onInst has it, computes it with Logic.replacedEval where the operand's tree says what LLVM answers: nullptr, RepOp, or a constant fold or a select's arm once the recursion has substituted; elsewhere the model hands over
delegates.isImpliedCondition: with LHSIsTrue=false, in simplifyOrInst on i1: with no Logic.Ext, the model hands over; with one, see rests_on. Logic.Ext.ofTerms answers nothing, as Oracle.none does for LHSIsTrue=true
